why: Out-of-order corruption, the expensive half: index 1 opens and then index 0 shows up. The canonical index is the call's position in the turn, so this stream is already wrong at its first frame — a turn whose first call claims position 1 is either missing a call or has had its fragments reordered, and nothing downstream can tell those apart. The refusal therefore lands on the opening frame, before a fragment nobody can place has been handed to the caller; the reordered continuation is never read at all, because the answer was sealed by then.
